fields.quoted_span: a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
fields.note: The requirement summary tracks the statute across the cap, small-landlord exception, service-member rules, inspections, photographs, 21-day return, electronic return, nonrefundable ban, bad-faith damages and successor liability. One minor gap: the summary says the 21-day return comes with invoices, receipts and photos, but the statute exempts deductions of $125 or less.

fields.quoted_span: No later than 21 calendar days after the tenant has vacated the premises
fields.note: The one-month cap, two-month small-landlord cap, service-member exclusion, 21-day return, $125 documentation exemption with the 14-day tenant request, and up to 2x bad-faith damages are all supported. The pre-July 2024 caps of 2 months unfurnished and 3 months furnished are not stated in D025. They are attributed to D007 and are not verifiable from this document.

fields.quoted_span: This subdivision shall not apply to a security collected or demanded by the landlord before July 1, 2024.
fields.note: The July 1, 2024 start for the one-month cap is confirmed, and so are the later April 1, 2025 and July 1, 2025 dates and the January 1, 2026 amendment effective date in the notes.

fields.quoted_span: (Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340, Sec. 1.   (AB 414)   Effective January 1, 2026.)
fields.note: The section is current text, amended effective January 1, 2026, with no repeal or sunset, which is consistent with in_force.

fields.quoted_span: This section applies to security for a rental agreement for residential property that is used as the dwelling of the tenant.
fields.note: The statewide residential scope, the pre-July 2024 carve-out, and the small-landlord conditions listed as unverifiable exemptions are all consistent with the text.

fields.quoted_span: (Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 340, Sec. 1.   (AB 414)   Effective January 1, 2026.)
fields.note: The document is California Civil Code section 1950.5, in Division 3, Part 4, Title 5, Chapter 2, and it shows the AB 414 and Stats. 2025, ch. 340 amendment. AB 12 is not named in D025, but it is listed only as an alias.
